newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares close weaker, Telecom seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close weaker, Telecom seen consolidating.

text.p: * NZ shares end weaker
* Market more subdued after Tuesday's sell-off
* Telecom seen consolidating ahead of 3rd qtr profit result ---------------------------(Feb 5)------------------------------
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
133 nil * NZSE-40 cap index -9.58 at 2,330.36
326 -2 * NZSC cap index +9.43 at 5,116.40
368 -1 * Volume NZ$43 million. Futures -4 at 1,176
706 -3 * Other movers - +12 -15
New Zealand shares closed weaker on Wednesday although trade was somewhat subdued after Tuesday's 1.6 percent sell-off, brokers said.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index fell 9.58 points to 2,330.36 on volume worth about NZ$43 million. The index is at its lowest since November.
Telecom, which shed 23 cents on Tuesday, dropped another three to $7.06.

Some brokers said they were a little surprised the market leader had not bounced back, especially after the company's announcement Tuesday afternoon that it would soon commence with its $1 billion share buyback.
But Nigel Scott at BZW said investors were a bit wary of Telecom ahead of its third quarter profit announcement on February 18.

Telecom's earnings forecasts have been downgraded by brokers. Reasons cited for the downgrades were a slowing New Zealand economy, litigation from competitor BellSouth and the writedown on Australian subsidiary Pacific Star, which Telecom
is in the process of selling off.
"Telecom, when it gets a bit of momentum going, tends to sometimes continue to go," Scott added.
However, he said Telecom was likely to consolidate now after its dramatic decline from $7.47 last week.
"I don't think anyone wants to knock it around too much more ahead of the result," he said.
Brokers said there had been good volume in Fletcher Paper, up two to $2.80, and in Carter Holt Harvey, which fell two cents to $3.25.
